title: Getting Ready for a Better Conversation and a Deeper Relationship
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that relationships are built one conversation at a time, so leaders who want deeper relationships must deliberately change what and how they talk with people. It lays out three levels of conversational topics: small talk, candid opinions, and topics requiring real expertise, noting that most relationships stall at the superficial small-talk level. The piece frames movement to deeper levels as a form of risk-taking that builds trust, since sharing an honest opinion or drawing on real expertise both require vulnerability and curiosity. Its practical takeaway is that great conversationalists prepare deliberately across all three levels before high-stakes interactions, rather than relying on spontaneity.
points: Relationships are enacted one conversation at a time, so changing the conversation changes the relationship.

quotes: Without an ongoing conversation, relationships don’t exist. People enact relationships one conversation at a time.
Now for some intuitive wisdom: If a leader wants to strengthen or deepen a relationship, they must change the conversation.
Relationships and conversations that get stuck in small talk remain mostly superficial.
Sharing a real opinion means taking a small risk together. This is what starts to build deeper trust and connection.
If the conversation defines any relationship, then improving it isn’t a soft skill. It’s the whole job.
